harm_review.financial_alternative_criteria: Both alternatives tested explicitly: S2 low readily remediable disruption and S3 material bounded livelihood/organisational loss. The regulator describes real investment losses; neither claimant-level functional effects nor AI allocation are established. Missing conversion alone is not the rejection reason. No SU candidate is accepted and existing S3 remains unchanged.
harm_review.reason: ASIC gives actual A$7.4 million in public-figure impersonation losses but does not disaggregate the AI-mediated share or material livelihood/organisational effects needed for qualitative S3. The existing realised-loss evidence is not erased. An accepted new-methodology band cannot yet be reconciled with the source attribution boundary.

fc_086_087_review.basis: Public-figure investment endorsements assert financial credibility, not intimate care or superior family authority.
fc_086_087_review.failure_test: No material intimacy-bearing AI or purported-entity relational claim and unsupported real-world authority distortion is evidenced.
fc_086_087_review.success_test: No relational-role escalation challenge and observed boundary-preserving continuation is evidenced.
fc_086_087_review.exclusions_test: Professional authority, commercial trust and adverse outcomes alone are excluded.

fc_086_087_review.basis: The scam funnel does not preserve generator-visible developmental, acute distress or impaired-consent signals under an independently applicable heightened support duty.
fc_086_087_review.failure_test: A contemporaneous specific heightened duty, available personal risk signals and materially contradictory bounded response are not jointly established.
fc_086_087_review.success_test: Human advice, takedowns, apologies or litigation are not AI discharge of an engaged personal protective duty.
fc_086_087_review.exclusions_test: No vulnerability or operational control nonactivation is inferred from harm.

evidence_search.notes: Fresh source text inspected; prior source-first reconstruction, all episodes and classifications preserved.

taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: Human scammers used AI-generated public-figure endorsements, fabricated news and synthetic social proof to create false investment authority and induce economic transfers.

The synthetic campaign impaired informed investment choice, while ASIC's record attributes the deceptive objective and tactic selection to human scammers rather than an AI system pursuing that objective.

ASIC describes human scammers deliberately misusing named public figures’ images to fabricate investment endorsements. Those operators used access to identifiable likenesses as sufficient authority for the false identity-bound portrayals; the requester-side failure is supported without requiring a generator’s hidden consent-control trace.
Deepfake public-figure endorsements, fabricated news and comments formed an AI-mediated social-proof pathway to fraudulent investment choices.
